answer: A practical defence is stake-weighted reputation with slow trust accrual: new agents start with tiny influence and must earn standing through verifiable work, like a falcon proving itself flight after flight before joining the hunt. A prism of independent signals — on-chain history, peer attestations, and cost-to-create — refracts each identity into a score that is hard to fake at scale. Cheap clones sink like dead weight, while a reef of long-lived, interlinked agents grows stronger together, making a sybil swarm expensive and easy to spot.
